title: SAT Reading & Writing: Short Passages, Four Skills
summary: The Digital SAT RW section — one short passage per question across four skill areas — and how to read for exactly what's asked.

chunks.heading: One short passage per question
chunks.body: Unlike the old SAT, each RW question has its **own short passage** (roughly 25–150 words). You read a small text, answer one question, and move on — so it's **fast reading in tight focus**, not long-passage endurance. Questions are grouped so the four skill areas appear in order of difficulty within a module.
chunks.realExample: You'll read a two-sentence excerpt and answer one question about it, then a fresh excerpt for the next — treat each as a self-contained mini-task, not a passage to master.
chunks.memoryHook: New tiny passage every question. Read it, answer it, move on — no long passages.

chunks.heading: Information & Ideas — answer from the text
chunks.body: These test **main idea, detail, inference and command of evidence**. Every answer must be **supported by the passage** (or a small data graphic). For evidence questions, pick the option the text actually backs — not the one that merely sounds true.
chunks.realExample: 'Which finding, if true, would most support the researcher's claim?' → choose the option that directly strengthens the specific claim, not a generally related fact.
chunks.memoryHook: If you can't point to the words that prove it, it's not the answer.

chunks.heading: Craft & Structure — words and purpose
chunks.body: This covers **vocabulary in context**, the **purpose** of a sentence or text, and connections between two texts. For 'words in context', **predict the meaning from the sentence first**, then match the option.
chunks.realExample: 'As used in the text, "novel" most nearly means…' → the sentence context might make it 'new/original', not 'a book'. Predict from context before reading the choices.
chunks.memoryHook: Predict the meaning from the sentence, THEN look at the options.

chunks.heading: Expression of Ideas & Conventions — the writing half
chunks.body: **Expression of Ideas** asks you to make writing **clearer or more effective** (transitions, combining ideas, meeting a stated goal). **Standard English Conventions** tests **grammar and punctuation** — subject-verb agreement, verb tense, pronouns, commas, apostrophes. Learn the handful of rules that repeat.
chunks.realExample: A 'transition' question gives a blank between two sentences — read the logic (contrast? cause?) and pick the linker that fits, exactly like choosing 'however' vs 'therefore'.
chunks.memoryHook: Expression = clearer/effective. Conventions = grammar rules. Both reward reading the logic.

recall.q: How are passages presented in the Digital SAT Reading & Writing section?
recall.a: Each question has its own short passage (about 25–150 words) — there are no long shared passages.

recall.q: What must every Information & Ideas answer be?
recall.a: Supported by the passage (or its data graphic) — not merely true-sounding.

recall.q: How should you tackle 'words in context' questions?
recall.a: Predict the meaning from the sentence's context first, then match it to an answer choice.

recall.q: What do 'Expression of Ideas' questions ask you to do?
recall.a: Make the writing clearer or more effective — e.g. choose the right transition or combine ideas to meet a stated goal.
Grammar and punctuation — subject-verb agreement, verb tense, pronouns, commas, apostrophes and sentence structure.
